subject.title: [bug]：Gateway pairing failure on Trim OS / TerraMaster NAS: WebSocket closes with code 1002 during device proof response

question: Should OpenClaw keep this Trim OS loopback CLI/cron path on the existing device pairing/token contract, or sponsor a new package-specific local auth bypass/config behavior?
rationale: The reported failure blocks Gateway access, but one requested workaround changes Gateway auth/device-pairing boundaries and another may be owned by the Trim OS package manager rather than core runtime.

options.title: Diagnose without bypass
options.body: Request sanitized connect-frame and Gateway-log proof, confirm CLI/Gateway protocol versions and package config regeneration, then repair diagnostics or package integration while preserving existing auth boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor a local bypass
options.body: Define an explicit loopback-only or package-owned bypass/config contract with security review, docs, audit behavior, and upgrade proof before implementation.

options.title: Route packaging externally
options.body: If source proof shows the Gateway behaves correctly and only the Trim OS manager rewrites config, keep core unchanged and send the config-regeneration fix to the package owner.

recommendation.title: Diagnose without bypass
recommendation.body: Request sanitized connect-frame and Gateway-log proof, confirm CLI/Gateway protocol versions and package config regeneration, then repair diagnostics or package integration while preserving existing auth boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail points to steipete for the core device auth/pairing contract and v3 payload refactor that any boundary decision would affect.
